site.title: Majestic 12
site.description: Practical guides on Majestic 12, organized for fast browsing and comparison.

pages.title: Alleged Mj 12 Documen
pages.summary: The alleged MJ-12 documents are a group of papers that claim a secret US committee, “Majestic 12” or “MJ-12”, was created after the 1947 Roswell incident to manage recovered extraterrestrial technology and bodies.

pages.title: Air Force
pages.summary: The Air Force determination cited by the FBI is one of the strongest official statements rejecting the principal MJ-12 document.

pages.title: Fabricated Finding
pages.summary: The 1988 record clearly shows that AFOSI rejected the circulated MJ-12 briefing, but it does not disclose every reason behind that judgment.

pages.title: AFOSI Role
pages.summary: AFOSI was consulted inside an active security inquiry, so its determination carried more investigative weight than a general public denial.

pages.title: Cutler Twining

pages.title: Missing Report
pages.summary: The public files preserve AFOSI's conclusion but not a detailed forensic report showing the searches, comparisons, and document tests behind it.

pages.title: Original Document
pages.summary: The released record describes circulating copies, leaving unresolved whether AFOSI ever conducted a physical examination of an original document.

pages.title: Scope of Verdict
pages.summary: AFOSI's finding is strongest when applied to the briefing then under review, not automatically to every alleged MJ-12 document that surfaced later.

pages.title: Anomaly Tests
pages.summary: A document can contain suspicious features without being conclusively forged, so the strength of each anomaly must be judged separately.

pages.title: Cutler Abroad
pages.summary: Cutler being overseas makes the disputed memorandum harder to explain, but an unsigned staff-prepared paper remains logically possible.

pages.title: Missing Records

pages.title: Security Marks

pages.title: 1984 Delivery

pages.title: Truman Signature

pages.title: Archive Provenance

pages.title: Custody vs Proof

pages.title: Truman Signature
pages.summary: A signature resembling one on a genuine Truman letter forced Friedman to explain why a reproduced signature might appear on an authentic briefing copy.

pages.title: Cooper Papers
pages.summary: The large body of MJ-12 papers linked to Timothy Cooper represents a separate provenance problem from the anonymously mailed core material.

pages.title: Burned Memo
pages.summary: The Burned Memo's dramatic cover letter cannot independently authenticate the document because its claims come from the same anonymous source chain.

pages.title: Cantwheel
pages.summary: The Cantwheel papers depend heavily on Cooper's account of an elderly former counter-intelligence source rather than a documented archival transfer.

pages.title: Chain of Custody
pages.summary: Without government-held originals or a documented transfer history, old paper, ink and typography cannot by themselves establish official provenance.

pages.title: Typewriter Dispute
pages.summary: Matching typographic quirks between Cooper's 1991 letters and the alleged annual report raised a direct question about possible common authorship.

pages.title: Cooper Papers Sub-Topic Index
pages.summary: Focused pages that expand on Cooper Papers.

pages.title: Marshall Forgery
pages.summary: The altered Marshall document shows how genuine wartime language could be repurposed to create a convincing false Majestic record.

pages.title: S 2 Batches
pages.summary: Hundreds of ordinary government pages in the S-2 batches can show access to old paperwork without validating extraordinary Majestic additions.

pages.title: Register Numbers
pages.summary: The Cutler-Twining memo lacks the register number expected for the Top Secret series where it was found.

pages.title: Air Force Rules
pages.summary: Air Force rules distinguished registered documents from other classified paperwork, so a missing number cannot serve as a universal forgery test.

pages.title: Register Numbers Sub-Topic Index
pages.summary: Focused pages that expand on Register Numbers.

pages.title: Lost Paperwork
pages.summary: A vanished cover sheet or control record could reconcile the memo with normal procedures, but the surviving file provides no direct evidence that one existed.

pages.title: How It Got
pages.summary: Ordinary misfiling and later insertion both fit the missing-number anomaly, but they imply very different histories for how the memo reached the archive.

pages.title: NARA Filing
pages.summary: The anomaly matters because NARA said this Air Force series was filed by Top Secret register number, making the memo an administrative mismatch.

pages.title: T4 1846
pages.summary: T4-1846 helped archivists locate the folder, but the disputed memo itself lacked the Top Secret register identifier expected in the series.

pages.title: 1954 Rules
pages.summary: Federal rules demanded strong accountability for Top Secret material, but they did not impose one identical visible numbering format on every document.

pages.title: Truman Timeline
pages.summary: The briefing claims Truman authorized Majestic-12 in September 1947, linking the committee's creation to the immediate post-Roswell period.

pages.summary: The timing is one of the more carefully fitted features of the alleged MJ-12 story. The purported Truman authorisation is dated 24 September 1947, only days after the Central Intelligence Agency formally came into existence and two days before the first meeting of the National Security Council (NSC). pages.title: Forrestal Role
pages.summary: Forrestal had been Secretary of Defense for only seven days when the alleged memo supposedly gave him responsibility for Operation Majestic Twelve.

pages.title: Roswell Gap
pages.summary: The supposed September authorization came about eleven weeks after Roswell, leaving a longer investigative interval than the phrase 'immediately after

pages.title: Security Reorg
pages.summary: The alleged order falls inside a remarkable week when the Defense Department, CIA and National Security Council were taking shape.

pages.title: Memo Sequence
pages.summary: The memo's reference to a 'recent conversation' raises a basic timing question because the authentic September 24 meeting has no recorded subject.

pages.title: Sept 24 Meeting
pages.summary: Truman really met James Forrestal and Vannevar Bush on September 24, but the surviving diary does not reveal what they discussed.

pages.title: Truman Memo
pages.summary: The alleged Truman memorandum raises a major question: does a reproduced signature indicate forgery or merely a copied official document?

pages.title: Freehand Vs Reproduc
pages.summary: The crucial question in the Truman–Forrestal signature dispute is not whether the disputed signature merely looks like Harry Truman's handwriting. Genuine signatures by the same person are expected to resemble one another.

pages.summary: Focused pages that expand on Truman Memo.

pages.title: Evidence Limits
pages.summary: The signature case is strong but limited because examiners worked from reproductions rather than an uncontested original MJ-12 sheet.

pages.title: Size Difference
pages.summary: A small size mismatch does not rule out copying because repeated photocopying can enlarge an otherwise matching signature image.

pages.title: Signing Device
pages.summary: Truman had used a multiple-pen signing device, but no evidence in the article ties that device to these two specific 1947 documents.

pages.title: Stray Mark
pages.summary: The shared accidental mark in Truman's signature is central to the claim that the MJ-12 image came from the Bush letter.

pages.title: T Stroke
pages.summary: Damage to the long T stroke is cited as evidence that typed words were removed from a donor signature before it was transplanted.
